m.x: A factory function that mixes all Matter.js physics components into any existing Phaser GameObject, including those you have extended or created yourself. This enables you to give anyGame Object full Matter physics capabilities without requiring it to extend a specific class.The following components are mixed directly onto the Game Object: Bounce, Collision, Force,Friction, Gravity, Mass, Sensor, SetBody, Sleep, Static, Transform, and Velocity. This meansmethods such as `setVelocity`, `setFriction`, and `isSensor` become available directly on theGame Object after this function is called.If `options` is an existing Matter Body instance (i.e. its `type` property equals `'body'`),that body is attached via `setExistingBody`. Otherwise, `options` is treated as a`MatterBodyConfig` and a new body is created via `setBody`, defaulting to a rectangle shapeif no `shape` property is provided.

p.x: The Matter world to add the body to.
The Game Object that will have the Matter body applied to it.
A Matter Body configuration object, or an instance of a Matter Body.
Should the newly created body be immediately added to the World?

r.x: The Game Object that was passed in, now enhanced with Matter physics components.
